`readboj` is an R client for official Bank of Japan (BOJ) statistics. It is
designed for workflows where the source response, parser schema, and
retrieval identity matter as much as the resulting values. The package can
read exact API series, search metadata, inspect official bulk files, and
discover dated Tankan comprehensive-data releases.

This article takes the shortest path to a useful result. Its default build
combines a verified rendering made from an official API response with small
synthetic fixtures that exercise the public parsers. Network retrieval remains
an explicit opt-in, so vignette and CRAN builds stay deterministic and offline.

## Load the package and discover databases

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 78)
library(readboj)

live <- identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")
chart_live <- live && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)

fixture_file <- function(name) {
  path <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "readboj")
  if (!nzchar(path)) {
    candidates <- c(file.path("inst", "extdata", name),
      file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", name))
    path <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)][1L]
  }
  if (!nzchar(path) || !file.exists(path)) stop("Fixture is unavailable: ", name)
  normalizePath(path, mustWork = TRUE)
}

figure_file <- function(name) {
  candidates <- c(
    file.path("man", "figures", name),
    file.path("..", "man", "figures", name),
    system.file("help", "figures", name, package = "readboj")
  )
  path <- candidates[nzchar(candidates) & file.exists(candidates)][1L]
  if (!length(path) || is.na(path)) stop("Figure is unavailable: ", name)
  path
}
```

```{r databases}
databases <- boj_databases()
databases[c(1L, 12L, 40L), c("db", "category_en", "name_en")]
```

`boj_databases()` is a local, revisioned registry. Its `db` values are the
identities accepted by the API; the bilingual names and category are useful
for presenting a choice to a user. The returned data frame also has
provenance, including the BOJ API-manual URL and source hash:

```{r database-provenance}
db_provenance <- boj_provenance(databases)
db_provenance[c("source", "source_url", "manual_revision", "database_count")]
```

## Retrieve and chart a time series

The following workflow searches official metadata, selects the exact monthly
exchange-rate series `FM08/FXERM07`, retrieves a closed 2025 period, keeps
valid `date` and `value` rows, and charts the result. Set
`READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true` to execute the bounded network path.
The default article build displays the checked-in rendering made from the
verified response recorded in `inst/NOTICE/boj-chart-source.txt`.

```{r retrieve-chart-data, eval=chart_live}
cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-chart-cache")
matches <- search_boj_series(
  query = "FXERM07", db = "FM08", language = "en", limit = 10L,
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
selected <- matches[matches$series_code == "FXERM07", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)

series <- read_boj_series(
  db = selected$db[[1]], code = selected$series_code[[1]],
  start_date = "202501", end_date = "202512", language = "en",
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
chart_data <- series[
  !is.na(series$date) & is.finite(series$value),
  c("date", "value")
]
stopifnot(nrow(chart_data) > 1L)
```

```{r retrieve-chart, eval=chart_live, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart of the monthly yen per U.S. dollar spot rate during 2025, falling through April and rising through December."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Yen per U.S. dollar in 2025",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Yen per U.S. dollar",
      caption = "Source: Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

```{r retrieve-chart-image, echo=FALSE, eval=!chart_live, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart of the monthly yen per U.S. dollar spot rate during 2025, falling through April and rising through December."}
knitr::include_graphics(figure_file("readboj-fxerm07-2025.png"))
```

The rendered series is *US.Dollar/Yen Spot Rate at 17:00 in JST, Average in
the Month, Tokyo Market*, measured in yen per U.S. dollar. The chart is a
readboj documentation illustration rather than an official BoJ chart or a
bundled raw-data snapshot. Use `boj_provenance(series)` after a live run to
retain the response URL, retrieval time, hashes, and query identity.

## Parse and inspect a saved response

For a completely reproducible first success, parse an exact local response
body with `read_boj_snapshot()`. This is the same normalised observation
schema used by the API reader, without a live request:

```{r first-success}
observations <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture_file("api-data-page-1.json"),
  type = "data_json",
  db = "FM08"
)
observations[, c(
  "db", "series_code", "frequency", "period", "date",
  "value", "raw_value", "value_status"
)]
```

The observation table keeps both the official period code and a parsed
`Date`. `value` is numeric where a value is present; a JSON `null` remains an
`NA_real_`, and `value_status` records that it was `"null"`. The `raw_value`
column is retained so a downstream transformation can distinguish a missing
source value from a value that was never returned.

The result is an ordinary data frame with stable columns and a provenance
attribute. Use `boj_provenance()` whenever a result is saved, joined, or
reported:

```{r first-provenance}
observation_provenance <- boj_provenance(observations)
observation_provenance[c(
  "source", "raw_sha256", "semantic_sha256", "bytes",
  "parser_schema"
)]
basename(observation_provenance$path)
```

The raw SHA-256 identifies the exact response bytes. For JSON, the semantic
hash is stable when only the volatile API `DATE` changes. This gives a small
but useful audit trail even for a local fixture.

## Reuse connected results offline

The retrieval shown in the chart workflow writes successful responses to its
bounded `cache_dir`. Repeating the same `read_boj_series()` call with
`offline = TRUE` replays a matching current snapshot without a network
request. Requests use HTTPS and official BoJ hosts, and the public API requires
no BoJ credentials. Typed `readboj_*` conditions distinguish unavailable
sources, transport failures, invalid responses, and configured resource
bounds.

For prescribed service wording and BOJ terms links, use:

```{r credit}
credit <- boj_api_credit()
credit[c("credit", "api_notice", "copyright", "service_release_contact")]
```

The package handles parsing and source identity; users remain responsible for
the BOJ service credit, release notification, and any downstream use of live
data.
